# py-markdown-table [![ci](https://github.com/hvalev/py-markdown-table/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/hvalev/py-markdown-table/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![codecov](https://codecov.io/gh/hvalev/py-markdown-table/branch/main/graph/badge.svg?token=ZZ8WXO4H6P)](https://codecov.io/gh/hvalev/py-markdown-table) [![Downloads](https://static.pepy.tech/badge/py-markdown-table)](https://pepy.tech/project/py-markdown-table) [![Downloads](https://static.pepy.tech/badge/py-markdown-table/month)](https://pepy.tech/project/py-markdown-table) [![Downloads](https://static.pepy.tech/badge/py-markdown-table/week)](https://pepy.tech/project/py-markdown-table) Tiny python library with zero dependencies which generates formatted multiline tables in `markdown`. ## Basic Use Install via pip as follows: ```bash pip install py-markdown-table ``` Pass a `list` of `dict`s where the `dict`s must have uniform keys which serve as column headers and the values are expanded to be rows. Simple example with no special formatting: ```python from py_markdown_table.markdown_table import markdown_table data = [ { "Product": "Smartphone", "Brand": "Apple", "Price": 999.99 }, { "Product": "Laptop", "Brand": "Dell", "Price": 1299.99 } ] markdown = markdown_table(data).get_markdown() print(markdown) ``` ``` +----------+-----+-------+ | Product |Brand| Price | +----------+-----+-------+ |Smartphone|Apple| 999.99| +----------+-----+-------+ | Laptop | Dell|1299.99| +----------+-----+-------+ ``` A more comprehensive example showcasing some of the formatting options: ```python from py_markdown_table.markdown_table import markdown_table jokes_list = [ { "joke1": "Why don't scientists trust atoms? Because they make up everything!", "joke2": "Did you hear about the mathematician who's afraid of negative numbers? He will stop at nothing to avoid them!", "joke3": "Why don't skeletons fight each other? They don't have the guts!" }, { "joke1": "What do you call a snowman with a six-pack? An abdominal snowman!", "joke2": "Why don't eggs tell jokes? Because they might crack up!", "joke3": "How does a penguin build its house? Igloos it together!" } ] markdown = markdown_table(jokes_list).set_params(padding_width = 3, padding_weight = 'centerleft', multiline = {'joke1': 30, 'joke2': 30, 'joke3': 30} ).get_markdown() ``` ``` +---------------------------------+---------------------------------+---------------------------------+ | joke1 | joke2 | joke3 | +---------------------------------+---------------------------------+---------------------------------+ | Why don't scientists trust | Did you hear about the | Why don't skeletons fight each | | atoms? Because they make up | mathematician who's afraid of | other? They don't have the | | everything! | negative numbers? He will stop | guts! | | | at nothing to avoid them! | | +---------------------------------+---------------------------------+---------------------------------+ | What do you call a snowman | Why don't eggs tell jokes? | How does a penguin build its | | with a six-pack? An abdominal | Because they might crack up! | house? Igloos it together! | | snowman! | | | +---------------------------------+---------------------------------+---------------------------------+ ``` You can also use pandas dataframes by formatting them as follows: ```python from py_markdown_table.markdown_table import markdown_table data = df.to_dict(orient='records') markdown_table(data).get_markdown() ``` ## Advanced Use To add parameters to how the markdown table is formatted, you can use the `set_params()` function on a `markdown_table` object, i.e. `markdown_table(data).set_params(...).get_markdown()`, which allows you to pass the following keyword arguments: ``` +-----------------------+---------------------+-------------------+--------------------------------+ | param | type | values | description | +-----------------------+---------------------+-------------------+--------------------------------+ | row_sep | str | | Row separation strategy using | | | | | `----` as pattern. Possible | | | | | values are: | +-----------------------+---------------------+-------------------+--------------------------------+ | | | always | Separate each row. | +-----------------------+---------------------+-------------------+--------------------------------+ | | | topbottom | Separate the top (header) and | | | | | bottom (last row) of the table.| +-----------------------+---------------------+-------------------+--------------------------------+ | | | markdown | Separate only the header from | | | | | the body. | +-----------------------+---------------------+-------------------+--------------------------------+ | | | None | No row separators will be | | | | | inserted. Defaults to "always".| +-----------------------+---------------------+-------------------+--------------------------------+ | padding_width | int or dict[str, | | Extra columns a column gets on | | | int] | | top of its widest cell. This is| | | | | one pool of slack per column, | | | | | not one per side - | | | | | `padding_weight` decides how | | | | | the pool is split between the | | | | | left and the right. Defaults to| | | | | `0`. Padding can also be | | | | | assigned per column by passing | | | | | key-value pairs whose keys are | | | | | exactly the columns of the | | | | | input data. | +-----------------------+---------------------+-------------------+--------------------------------+ | padding_weight | str or dict[str, | | How the `padding_width` of a | | | str] | | column is distributed between | | | | | its left and its right side. | | | | | Can be assigned globally for | | | | | the whole table as a string or | | | | | per-column by passing key-value| | | | | pairs whose keys are exactly | | | | | the columns of the input data. | | | | | Possible values are: | +-----------------------+---------------------+-------------------+--------------------------------+ | | | left | Aligns the cell's contents to | | | | | the end of the cell. | +-----------------------+---------------------+-------------------+--------------------------------+ | | | right | Aligns the cell's contents to | | | | | the beginning of the cell. | +-----------------------+---------------------+-------------------+--------------------------------+ | | | centerleft | Centers cell's contents with | | | | | extra padding allocated to the | | | | | beginning of the cell. | +-----------------------+---------------------+-------------------+--------------------------------+ | | | centerright | Centers cell's contents with | | | | | extra padding allocated to the | | | | | end of the cell. | +-----------------------+---------------------+-------------------+--------------------------------+ | padding_char | str | | Single character used to fill | | | | | padding. Default is a blank | | | | | space ` `. | +-----------------------+---------------------+-------------------+--------------------------------+ | newline_char | str | | Character appended to each row | | | | | to force a newline. Default is | | | | | ` `. | +-----------------------+---------------------+-------------------+--------------------------------+ | float_rounding | int | | Number of digits to keep after | | | | | the decimal point of `float` | | | | | cells, rounding them to that | | | | | precision. Must be 0 or | | | | | greater; `None` leaves floats | | | | | untouched. | +-----------------------+---------------------+-------------------+--------------------------------+ | emoji_spacing | str | | Strategy for rendering | | | | | characters that a monospace | | | | | font draws two columns wide. | +-----------------------+---------------------+-------------------+--------------------------------+ | multiline | dict[str, int] | | Wrap columns to the given | | | | | widths, as a dictionary with a | | | | | width per column. The width is | | | | | the space left for content, so | | | | | `padding_width` is added on top| | | | | of it rather than taken from | | | | | it. Values must be provided for| | | | | every column. | +-----------------------+---------------------+-------------------+--------------------------------+ | multiline_strategy | str | | Strategy applied to rendering | | | | | contents in multiple lines. | | | | | Possible values are: | +-----------------------+---------------------+-------------------+--------------------------------+ | | | rows | Splits only rows overfilling | | | | | the predefined column width. | +-----------------------+---------------------+-------------------+--------------------------------+ | | | header | Splits only the header | | | | | overfilling the predefined | | | | | column width. | +-----------------------+---------------------+-------------------+--------------------------------+ | | | rows_and_header | Splits rows and header | | | | | overfilling the predefined | | | | | column width. | +-----------------------+---------------------+-------------------+--------------------------------+ | multiline_delimiter | str | | Character a cell's contents are| | | | | split on to find places to | | | | | wrap, and put back between the | | | | | parts that end up on one line. | +-----------------------+---------------------+-------------------+--------------------------------+ | quote | bool | | Wraps the generated markdown | | | | | table in block quotes ` | | | | | ```table``` `. | +-----------------------+---------------------+-------------------+--------------------------------+ | compact | bool | | Emit the smallest table that is| | | | | still valid markdown: cells are| | | | | not padded and the header | | | | | separator is a single `-` per | | | | | column. Only meaningful when | | | | | the renderer draws the table, | | | | | so it requires `row_sep` | | | | | `markdown`. Widths given to | | | | | `multiline` are still honoured,| | | | | they just no longer add | | | | | padding. Default is `False`. | +-----------------------+---------------------+-------------------+--------------------------------+ ``` ## Type hints The package ships a `py.typed` marker and every function is annotated, so `mypy` and IDEs see `markdown_table(data).set_params(...)` returning the same type it takes and reject a plain `dict` where a list of rows is expected. ## Utils The namespace `py_markdown_table.utils` provides `count_emojis()`, `find_longest_contiguous_strings()` and `split_list_by_indices()`. `count_emojis()` reports the characters in a string that a monospace font draws two columns wide - emoji and CJK among them - together with their position, which is what `emoji_spacing` uses. `find_longest_contiguous_strings()` finds the longest string in each column that cannot be broken, which is the width you have to give that column for `multiline` to accept it. `split_list_by_indices()` cuts a string at given offsets and is what the wrapping code uses to treat a wide character as its own break opportunity. ## Further Examples All the examples below render this data: ```python data = [ {"title": "Vrij Zwemmen", "time": "21:30-23:00", "date": "Wed 09.12", "seats": "24/24"}, {"title": "Vrij Zwemmen", "time": "12:00-13:00", "date": "Thu 10.12", "seats": "18/18"}, {"title": "Vrij Zwemmen", "time": "7:30-8:30", "date": "Fri 11.12", "seats": "18/18"}, {"title": "Vrij Zwemmen", "time": "13:15-14:15", "date": "Sat 12.12", "seats": "18/18"}, ] ``` ## Further Examples ### Row separatation ```python markdown_table(data).set_params(row_sep = 'always').get_markdown() ```
see example ``` +------------+-----------+---------+-----+ | title | time | date |seats| +------------+-----------+---------+-----+ |Vrij Zwemmen|21:30-23:00|Wed 09.12|24/24| +------------+-----------+---------+-----+ |Vrij Zwemmen|12:00-13:00|Thu 10.12|18/18| +------------+-----------+---------+-----+ |Vrij Zwemmen| 7:30-8:30 |Fri 11.12|18/18| +------------+-----------+---------+-----+ |Vrij Zwemmen|13:15-14:15|Sat 12.12|18/18| +------------+-----------+---------+-----+ ```

```python markdown_table(data).set_params(row_sep = 'topbottom').get_markdown() ```
see example ``` +------------+-----------+---------+-----+ | title | time | date |seats| |Vrij Zwemmen|21:30-23:00|Wed 09.12|24/24| |Vrij Zwemmen|12:00-13:00|Thu 10.12|18/18| |Vrij Zwemmen| 7:30-8:30 |Fri 11.12|18/18| |Vrij Zwemmen|13:15-14:15|Sat 12.12|18/18| +------------+-----------+---------+-----+ ```

```python markdown_table(data).set_params(row_sep = 'markdown').get_markdown() ```
see example ``` | title | time | date |seats| |------------|-----------|---------|-----| |Vrij Zwemmen|21:30-23:00|Wed 09.12|24/24| |Vrij Zwemmen|12:00-13:00|Thu 10.12|18/18| |Vrij Zwemmen| 7:30-8:30 |Fri 11.12|18/18| |Vrij Zwemmen|13:15-14:15|Sat 12.12|18/18| ```

```python markdown_table(data).set_params(row_sep = 'markdown', quote = False).get_markdown() ```
see example | title | time | date |seats| |------------|-----------|---------|-----| |Vrij Zwemmen|21:30-23:00|Wed 09.12|24/24| |Vrij Zwemmen|12:00-13:00|Thu 10.12|18/18| |Vrij Zwemmen| 7:30-8:30 |Fri 11.12|18/18| |Vrij Zwemmen|13:15-14:15|Sat 12.12|18/18|

### Padding, padding weight and padding char ```python markdown_table(data).set_params(row_sep = 'topbottom', padding_width = 5, padding_weight = 'left').get_markdown() ```
see example ``` +-----------------+----------------+--------------+----------+ | title| time| date| seats| | Vrij Zwemmen| 21:30-23:00| Wed 09.12| 24/24| | Vrij Zwemmen| 12:00-13:00| Thu 10.12| 18/18| | Vrij Zwemmen| 7:30-8:30| Fri 11.12| 18/18| | Vrij Zwemmen| 13:15-14:15| Sat 12.12| 18/18| +-----------------+----------------+--------------+----------+ ```

```python markdown_table(data).set_params(row_sep = 'topbottom', padding_width = 5, padding_weight = 'centerright').get_markdown() ```
see example ``` +-----------------+----------------+--------------+----------+ | title | time | date | seats | | Vrij Zwemmen | 21:30-23:00 | Wed 09.12 | 24/24 | | Vrij Zwemmen | 12:00-13:00 | Thu 10.12 | 18/18 | | Vrij Zwemmen | 7:30-8:30 | Fri 11.12 | 18/18 | | Vrij Zwemmen | 13:15-14:15 | Sat 12.12 | 18/18 | +-----------------+----------------+--------------+----------+ ```

```python markdown_table(data).set_params(row_sep = 'always', padding_width = 5, padding_weight = 'centerright', padding_char = '.').get_markdown() ```
see example ``` +-----------------+----------------+--------------+----------+ |......title......|......time......|.....date.....|..seats...| +-----------------+----------------+--------------+----------+ |..Vrij Zwemmen...|..21:30-23:00...|..Wed 09.12...|..24/24...| +-----------------+----------------+--------------+----------+ |..Vrij Zwemmen...|..12:00-13:00...|..Thu 10.12...|..18/18...| +-----------------+----------------+--------------+----------+ |..Vrij Zwemmen...|...7:30-8:30....|..Fri 11.12...|..18/18...| +-----------------+----------------+--------------+----------+ |..Vrij Zwemmen...|..13:15-14:15...|..Sat 12.12...|..18/18...| +-----------------+----------------+--------------+----------+ ```

```python markdown_table(data).set_params(row_sep = 'always', padding_width = 5, padding_weight = 'centerright', padding_char = '.').get_markdown() ```
see example ``` +-----------------+----------------+--------------+----------+ |......title......|......time......|.....date.....|..seats...| +-----------------+----------------+--------------+----------+ |..Vrij Zwemmen...|..21:30-23:00...|..Wed 09.12...|..24/24...| +-----------------+----------------+--------------+----------+ |..Vrij Zwemmen...|..12:00-13:00...|..Thu 10.12...|..18/18...| +-----------------+----------------+--------------+----------+ |..Vrij Zwemmen...|...7:30-8:30....|..Fri 11.12...|..18/18...| +-----------------+----------------+--------------+----------+ |..Vrij Zwemmen...|..13:15-14:15...|..Sat 12.12...|..18/18...| +-----------------+----------------+--------------+----------+ ```

### Per-column padding and padding weight ```python markdown_table(data).set_params(row_sep = 'always', padding_width = {"title": 2, "time": 4, "date": 3, "seats": 1}, padding_weight = {"title": "left", "time": "right", "date": "centerleft", "seats": "centerright"}).get_markdown() ```
see example ``` +--------------+---------------+------------+------+ | title|time | date |seats | +--------------+---------------+------------+------+ | Vrij Zwemmen|21:30-23:00 | Wed 09.12 |24/24 | +--------------+---------------+------------+------+ | Vrij Zwemmen|12:00-13:00 | Thu 10.12 |18/18 | +--------------+---------------+------------+------+ | Vrij Zwemmen|7:30-8:30 | Fri 11.12 |18/18 | +--------------+---------------+------------+------+ | Vrij Zwemmen|13:15-14:15 | Sat 12.12 |18/18 | +--------------+---------------+------------+------+ ```

The last example sizes three columns, so its per-column dicts line up with its data: ```python data = [ {"A": "row1_A and additional stuff", "B": "row1_B", "C": "row1_C"}, {"A": "row2_A", "B": "row2_B and additional stuff", "C": "row2_C"}, {"A": "row3_A", "B": "row3_B", "C": "row3_C"}, ] ``` ```python markdown_table(data).set_params(row_sep = 'always', padding_width = {"A": 2, "B": 4, "C": 3}, padding_weight = {"A": "left", "B": "right", "C": "centerleft"}).get_markdown() ```
see example ``` +-----------------------------+-------------------------------+---------+ | A|B | C | +-----------------------------+-------------------------------+---------+ | row1_A and additional stuff|row1_B | row1_C | +-----------------------------+-------------------------------+---------+ | row2_A|row2_B and additional stuff | row2_C | +-----------------------------+-------------------------------+---------+ | row3_A|row3_B | row3_C | +-----------------------------+-------------------------------+---------+ ```

### Compact output When a markdown renderer draws the table, the padding and the long separator are only costing you characters. `compact=True` drops both and leaves the smallest table that is still valid markdown, which matters when the output goes into a field with a size limit. It needs `row_sep="markdown"`, because where the characters themselves form the borders an unpadded table is unreadable. ```python data = [ {"_time": "2025-10-03T12:54:42.000+00:00", "field1": "text text", "field2": "aa bb cc"}, {"_time": "2025-10-04T09:15:00.000+00:00", "field1": "more text", "field2": "dd ee ff"}, ] ``` ```python markdown_table(data).set_params(row_sep = "markdown", quote = False, compact = True).get_markdown() ```
see example ``` |_time|field1|field2| |-|-|-| |2025-10-03T12:54:42.000+00:00|text text|aa bb cc| |2025-10-04T09:15:00.000+00:00|more text|dd ee ff| ```

### Multiline and emoji Wrapping needs a width per column, and the first two examples use: ```python data = [ {"A": "row1_A and additional stuff", "B": "row1_B", "C": "row1_C"}, {"A": "row2_A", "B": "row2_B and additional stuff", "C": "row2_C"}, {"A": "row3_A", "B": "row3_B", "C": "row3_C"}, ] ``` ```python markdown_table(data).set_params(padding_width = 0, padding_weight = "centerleft", multiline = {"A": 25, "B": 12, "C": 9}).get_markdown() ```
see example ``` +-------------------------+------------+---------+ | A | B | C | +-------------------------+------------+---------+ | row1_A and additional | row1_B | row1_C | | stuff | | | +-------------------------+------------+---------+ | row2_A | row2_B and | row2_C | | | additional | | | | stuff | | +-------------------------+------------+---------+ | row3_A | row3_B | row3_C | +-------------------------+------------+---------+ ```

```python markdown_table(data).set_params(padding_width = 2, padding_weight = "centerleft", multiline = {"A": 25, "B": 12, "C": 9}).get_markdown() ```
see example ``` +---------------------------+--------------+-----------+ | A | B | C | +---------------------------+--------------+-----------+ | row1_A and additional | row1_B | row1_C | | stuff | | | +---------------------------+--------------+-----------+ | row2_A | row2_B and | row2_C | | | additional | | | | stuff | | +---------------------------+--------------+-----------+ | row3_A | row3_B | row3_C | +---------------------------+--------------+-----------+ ```

```python data = [ {"those are multi rows": "yes they are"}, {"those are multi rows": "no they are not"}, ] ``` ```python markdown_table(data).set_params(row_sep = "always", multiline = {"those are multi rows": 5}, multiline_strategy = "rows_and_header").get_markdown() ```
see example ``` +-----+ |those| | are | |multi| | rows| +-----+ | yes | | they| | are | +-----+ | no | | they| | are | | not | +-----+ ```

```python data = [ {"title that is maybe too long": "Vrij Zwemmen", "time": "21:30-23:00", "date": "\U0001f60a", "seats": "24/24"}, {"title that is maybe too long": "Vrij Zwemmen", "time": "12:00-13:00", "date": "Thu 10.12", "seats": "18/18"}, {"title that is maybe too long": "Vrij Zwemmen", "time": "7:30-8:30", "date": "Fri 11.12", "seats": "\U0001f60a\U0001f30d\U0001f389"}, {"title that is maybe too long": "Vrij Zwemmen", "time": "13:15-14:15", "date": "Sat 12.12", "seats": "20/20"}, {"title that is maybe too long": "Vrij Zwemmen", "time": "7:30-8:30", "date": "Fri 11.12", "seats": " asd \U0001f60a-\U0001f30d:\U0001f389"}, {"title that is maybe too long": "Zwemmen", "time": "13:15-14:15", "date": "Sat 12.12", "seats": "20/20"}, ] ``` ```python markdown_table(data).set_params(row_sep = "topbottom", emoji_spacing = "mono", multiline = {"title that is maybe too long": 7, "time": 11, "date": 5, "seats": 5,}, multiline_strategy = "rows_and_header").get_markdown() ```
see example *Note:* Github's markdown preview does not render emojis as two whole characters, hence the slight offsets in cells containing emojis. ``` +-------+-----------+-----+-----+ | title | time | date|seats| |that is| | | | | maybe | | | | | too | | | | | long | | | | | Vrij |21:30-23:00| 😊 |24/24| |Zwemmen| | | | | Vrij |12:00-13:00| Thu |18/18| |Zwemmen| |10.12| | | Vrij | 7:30-8:30 | Fri | 😊🌍| |Zwemmen| |11.12| 🎉 | | Vrij |13:15-14:15| Sat |20/20| |Zwemmen| |12.12| | | Vrij | 7:30-8:30 | Fri | asd | |Zwemmen| |11.12| 😊- | | | | |🌍:🎉| |Zwemmen|13:15-14:15| Sat |20/20| | | |12.12| | +-------+-----------+-----+-----+ ``` Below is an example from a monospaced terminal, where the table is rendered correctly. ![Table with emoji in terminal](res/table_w_emoji.jpg)
## Benchmarks The table below provide some benchmark results, evaluating the performance on data containing incrementally larger number of `columns`, `rows`, and characters in each table cell (i.e. `cell_size`). You can benchmark it on your own system using the script contained within `utils/benchmark.py`. Generally, reasonably-sized tables intended to be read by a human can be generated within a millisecond.
see benchmark ``` +----------------+-----------+---------------+ | parameters | Multiline | speed | +----------------+-----------+---------------+ | columns: 2 | False | 0.191895 ms | | rows: 10 | | | | cell_size: 5 | | | +----------------+-----------+---------------+ | columns: 4 | False | 0.251465 ms | | rows: 40 | | | | cell_size: 20 | | | +----------------+-----------+---------------+ | columns: 8 | False | 1.875732 ms | | rows: 160 | | | | cell_size: 80 | | | +----------------+-----------+---------------+ | columns: 16 | False | 22.107422 ms | | rows: 640 | | | | cell_size: 320 | | | +----------------+-----------+---------------+ | columns: 2 | True | 0.149902 ms | | rows: 10 | | | | cell_size: 5 | | | +----------------+-----------+---------------+ | columns: 4 | True | 0.463379 ms | | rows: 40 | | | | cell_size: 20 | | | +----------------+-----------+---------------+ | columns: 8 | True | 6.229248 ms | | rows: 160 | | | | cell_size: 80 | | | +----------------+-----------+---------------+ | columns: 16 | True | 137.902100 ms | | rows: 640 | | | | cell_size: 320 | | | +----------------+-----------+---------------+ ```
